market_question: Will France send warships through the Strait of Hormuz by May 31, 2026?
reasoning: France maintains a consistent naval presence in the Gulf region, including periodic transits through the Strait of Hormuz for freedom of navigation, anti-piracy, and escort operations. Historical activity and ongoing geopolitical tensions make at least one French warship transit highly plausible within the next year, far exceeding the 3.6% implied probability.
evidence_points: France has regularly deployed frigates to the Arabian Sea and Persian Gulf, often transiting the Strait of Hormuz as part of multinational (CMF) or EU missions.
Even after the perceived wind-down of EMASoH, French assets remain in the region for broader security duties, and a routine transit is likely.
Official confirmation or credible reporting of a French warship transit is easy to trigger under resolution rules, given typical defense media coverage.
